land.text: Cliopatria draws its 1241 Granada shape (114 of 120 cells) inside the Almohad Caliphate's 1236-1240 shape

predecessors.note: The pages opened name no overlord for Arjona, Jaén, Guadix, Baeza, Granada or Málaga when they accepted Muhammad I (1232-1239); Cliopatria's Almohad shape is the only polity covering them, which is why it is listed. A gap-filler should settle who held the land (the Muhammad I page speaks of 'Ibn Hud's rule').
Cliopatria's Taifa of Almería row (1015-1249) overlaps the emirate by 6 cells in 1236-1240 and then lapses; the page does not name Almería's previous ruler.

land.text: Granada, Almería, Guadix and Baza, added to Cliopatria's Crown of Castile in 1492

successors.note: 'On 2 January 1492, Boabdil surrendered Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella'; the Treaty of Granada was signed on 25 November 1491. Infobox 'Territorial changes: Granada annexed to Castile'.

capitals.name: Arjona
capitals.note: Seat of the proclamation only: 'On 16 July 1232, a mosque assembly in Arjona declared the town's independence.' The page names no capital before Granada.

capitals.name: Granada
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Granada'; the Muhammad I page: he took Granada 'which he then made his capital' (May 1237 or May 1238 on that page, 17 April 1238 on the Emirate page).

rulers.name: Muhammad XII (al-Zaghal)
rulers.title: rival emir
rulers.note: The Nasrid table gives 1485-1486; the Emirate page has him losing Málaga in 1487 and holding Baza, Guadix and Almería until his surrender.

rulers.name: Muhammad XI (Boabdil), second reign
rulers.note: The table gives 1486-1492 (its family tree 1487-1492); 'On 2 January 1492, Boabdil surrendered Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella.' Rows 21 and 23 of the page's table are absent.

correction.text: Arjona, Jaén and Guadix, the towns that accepted Muhammad I in 1232 (Baeza is left out: see the note)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1232-1237: Cliopatria's first Granada shape is 1241, but the infobox gives 'Established: 1232' and 'On 16 July 1232 ... Arjona' proclaimed Muhammad I, with Jaén, Guadix and Baeza, which 'accepted his authority quickly in 1232'. Granada itself was only stormed on 17 April 1238 (Muhammad I page: May 1237 or May 1238), so the early realm is the Jaén-Arjona-Guadix strip, not the later core. Baeza is named on the page but left out: the Castile dossier's page (Ferdinand III) has Castilian forces occupying Baeza, Andújar and Martos from 1225, and Cliopatria's Castile shape holds the Jaén district from 1236.

correction.text: the 1232 towns plus Granada and Almería

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1238: Granada ('a revolt successfully stormed the city's citadel on 17 April 1238') and Almería ('accepted him in 1238') join the Jaén-Guadix realm.

correction.text: the 1238 realm plus Málaga

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1239-1240: 'He also took Almería in 1238 and Málaga in 1239'; the Emirate page says Málaga came 'in 1238 or 1239'. Jaén and Arjona are still his until 1246 and 1244.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1241 shape plus Jaén and Arjona, held until 1246 and 1244

keyframe_review.note: 31,457 km2 for 1241-1249 (the Emirate page gives no area; its core 'roughly correspond[s] to the modern Spanish provinces of Granada, Almería, and Málaga', 104 gazetteer cells against the shape's 120). Cliopatria's Castile row already holds the Jaén district and Arjona from 1236, but the Muhammad I page has Castile capture Arjona in 1244 and Jaén surrender in March 1246. The shape is therefore too small before 1244/1246; this verdict covers 1241-1243.

correction.text: the 1241 shape plus Jaén, without Arjona

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1244-1245: 'In 1244, Castile besieged and captured Muhammad's hometown of Arjona'; Jaén still holds until the March 1246 treaty.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1241 shape, unchanged, for 1246-1249

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1246-1249: after the Treaty of Jaén (March 1246, 'to surrender Jaén and to become Ferdinand's vassal') the emirate is exactly Cliopatria's 1241 outline.

31,429 km2 for 1250-1293: three cells swapped against 1241 (a cell near Alcalá la Real gained, two on the eastern edge lost). The Muhammad I page gives the emirate at his death in 1273 as 'spanned 240 miles (390 km) between Tarifa in the west and eastern frontiers beyond Almería', which the outline fits. The Marinid occupation of Algeciras, Tarifa and Ronda (1275) and of Málaga (1278-1279) are not in any Cliopatria shape; the ledger carries them.

31,106 km2: one cell moves in the Strait. Abu Ya'qub 'ceded Algeciras and Ronda to the Nasrids' in 1294 and Castile captured Tarifa in October 1292 and kept it (Emirate page). The Strait cells (Gibraltar to Tarifa) stay in Granada's shape through 1462 although the History of Gibraltar page has Castile holding Gibraltar 1309-1333 and the Marinids 1333-1374; the ledger events of 1309, 1333 and 1374 override the shape there. This verdict covers 1294-1326. Ronda and Marbella (1327) and Algeciras (1328) went to the Marinids and the Olvera line (1327) and Teba (1330) to Castile, none of it in this shape: the new keyframes 1327, 1328 and 1330 carry it (eu-12-l repair, 2026-10-25).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1294 shape, unchanged, for 1294-1326; from 1327 see the new keyframes

union.text: Olvera, Pruna, Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime (no gazetteer entries)

correction.text: the 1294 shape without Ronda and Marbella (ceded to the Marinids in 1327) and the Olvera line (taken by Castile in June 1327)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1327: Emirate page, Muhammad IV 'ceded Ronda and Algeciras again in 1327 and 1328, respectively'; Muhammad IV page: 'he had to surrender Ronda and Marbella' and 'the capture of Olvera, in June 1327'. The cells for Ronda, Marbella and Olvera are circles round the towns (no gazetteer entries for Ronda and the Olvera line).

union.text: Olvera, Pruna, Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime (no gazetteer entries)

correction.text: the 1294 shape without Ronda, Marbella, Algeciras (all Marinid) and the Olvera line (Castile)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1328-1329: Algeciras joins Ronda with the Marinids ('in 1327 and 1328, respectively'; 'followed by Algeciras in the next year', Muhammad IV page). The Siege of Algeciras page has the King of Morocco take the city over in 1329.

union.text: Olvera, Pruna, Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime (no gazetteer entries)

correction.text: the 1294 shape without Ronda, Marbella, Algeciras (Marinid) and the Olvera line and Teba (Castile)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1330-1332: Teba surrendered to Castile on 30 August 1330 (Muhammad IV page: 'the fortress surrendered on 30 August'). Gibraltar (Castilian 1309 to June 1333) stays in the shape and is carried by the ledger, as in the earlier keyframes.

30,045 km2: one cell gained near Málaga and five lost on the northern frontier (Castile's 1333 gain, 5 cells between 37.0 and 37.2 N, -5.3 and -4.9 E, the Olvera-Teba line). The Alfonso XI page, opened for exactly this, dates only the Battle of Río Salado (1340), Algeciras (1344) and the 1349-1350 siege of Gibraltar and is silent on conquests from Granada in the 1320s-1330s, so the move is undated (unverified). Gibraltar itself 'surrendered to the Moors of Fez' in 1333 in a 'joint Nasrid-Marinid effort' (History of Gibraltar). Corrected by the eu-12-l repair: Ronda and Marbella (1327) and Algeciras (1328) belong to the Marinids until the 1344 keyframe (Algeciras) and 1374 (Ronda, Marbella); the Olvera line is dated 1327 and Teba 1330 (Muhammad IV page), so the 'undated' remark above no longer holds. Gibraltar stays in the shape and is carried by the ledger.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1333 shape without Ronda, Marbella and Algeciras, which stay with the Marinids
Cliopatria's 1344 shape without Ronda and Marbella (Marinid), holding from 1342 (Priego and Alcalá la Real); Algeciras is not Granada's here

keyframe_review.note: 28,333 km2 for 1344-1351: seven cells go to Castile (two on the Strait coast, five along 37.3 N between -4.3 and -3.8 E, which is the Priego-Alcalá la Real line). Castile captured Priego and Alcalá la Real in 1342 and Algeciras surrendered on 26 March 1344, so the loss starts in 1342; the shape is unchanged. Corrected by the eu-12-l repair: Algeciras was Marinid from 1328/1329, so the two Strait cells that Cliopatria hands to Castile in 1344 were not a Granadan loss (the ledger event of 26 March 1344 was removed; the siege stays in wars[]); Ronda and Marbella stay out of the shape until 1374.

28,062 km2: one eastern cell near 37.7 N, -3.0 E moves to Castile; no page opened mentions it (unverified: page budget). Ronda and Marbella are removed because they were Marinid until the bridged return of 1374 (ledger; eu-12-l repair).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1352 shape without Ronda and Marbella (Marinid)
the 1352 shape without Ronda and Marbella (Marinid), for 1363-1368

keyframe_review.note: 30,045 km2 for 1363-1374: Cliopatria hands back eight cells (the seven of 1344 and the eastern one). The pages opened say Castile took Priego and Alcalá la Real in 1342 and Algeciras in 1344 and that 'Muhammed V, Sultan of Granada, took the opportunity to recapture Al-Jazeera Al-Khadra' in 1369; nothing returns Priego or Alcalá la Real. The 1352 outline therefore holds for 1363-1368 and Algeciras is added from 1369 (next keyframe). Ronda and Marbella stay out of the shape until 1374 (ledger; eu-12-l repair).

correction.text: the 1352 shape plus Algeciras (recaptured in 1369), without Ronda and Marbella (Marinid)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1369-1373: 'Muhammed V, Sultan of Granada, took the opportunity to recapture Al-Jazeera Al-Khadra' (1369); the Moors destroyed the city in 1379 (paraphrase of the page). Gibraltar returns to Granada in 1374 (History of Gibraltar: 'In 1374 the latter handed the peninsula to the former', the Marinids to the Nasrids). Ends in 1373 (eu-12-l repair): Ronda and Marbella return in 1374 (bridge), see the next keyframe.

correction.text: the 1352 shape plus Algeciras, with Ronda and Marbella back from the Marinids

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1374-1378: the Marinids hand Gibraltar to Granada in 1374 ('In 1374 the latter handed the peninsula to the former', History of Gibraltar) and Ronda and Marbella are bridged back in the same year (ledger, confidence 1). The Moors destroy Algeciras in 1379.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1375 shape, unchanged, holding from 1379

keyframe_review.note: 28,062 km2 for 1375-1401, the 1352 outline again. Valid from 1379, when the Moors destroyed the city of Algeciras; for 1375-1378 the 1374 keyframe applies.

28,037 km2: two cells swap on the northwest edge (Setenil-Zahara side). The Emirate page dates a 'War with Castile ... between 1405 and 1410' but no loss there; unverified: page budget. The Zahara de la Sierra page now dates the Setenil-Zahara edge: Zahara 'ruled by Arabs until 1407' (ledger; eu-12-l repair); Setenil is on no page opened.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1415 shape, unchanged, holding from 1410

keyframe_review.note: 27,839 km2: the cell at Antequera (-4.8 E, 37.1 N) goes to Castile. 'He conquered the town of Antequera (1410)', five years before the shape, so the loss starts in 1410; the shape is unchanged.
27,296 km2: two cells lost and one gained on the north-eastern edge (37.8 N, -2.9 to -2.5 E). No page opened dates it (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1463 shape, unchanged, holding 1462-1481

keyframe_review.note: 26,052 km2: five cells along the Gibraltar-Algeciras coast go to Castile. 'Moorish rule over Gibraltar came to an end in August 1462', so the loss starts in 1462, a year before the shape. Holds to 1481; the Granada War begins with Zahara (26 December 1481) and Alhama (February 1482).

correction.text: the 1463 shape without Alhama de Granada

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1482-1484: 'The seizure of Alhama ... is usually said to be the formal beginning of the Granada War' (infobox: February 1482). Cliopatria keeps the 1463 outline until 1487.

correction.text: the 1463 shape without Alhama, Ronda and Marbella

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1485: 'Ronda fell to him after fifteen days' and 'Ronda's fall allowed Marbella, a base of the Granadan fleet, to come into Christian hands next' (1485).

correction.text: the 1463 shape without Alhama, Ronda, Marbella and Loja

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1486: the page mentions a 'second Loja siege' in 1486; the page does not state the surrender, so Loja's fall in 1486 is my reading.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1487 shape, unchanged, holding 1487-1489

keyframe_review.note: 13,011 km2 for 1487-1491: Cliopatria removes 48 cells (Ronda, Marbella, Málaga, Vélez-Málaga, Loja, Alhama) in 1487; 'Vélez-Málaga capitulated on 27 April 1487' and Málaga fell on 18 August 1487 after a siege from 7 May. The remaining eastern emirate (Baza, Guadix, Almería, the Granada Vega) holds only until 1489: 'after six months, al-Zagal surrendered' at Baza (siege begun 1489), and he 'negotiated the surrender of Almería and Guadix' (Emirate page, no date).

correction.text: the city of Granada and its Vega (the remnant after Baza, Guadix and Almería)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1490-1491: only the city of Granada and its surroundings remain: 'An eight-month siege of Granada began in April 1491'; the Treaty of Granada was signed on 25 November 1491 and 'the city capitulated on January 2, 1492'. The remnant is my reading (Cliopatria's 1487 outline within 60 km of Granada), not a page's boundary.

region.text: Arjona, where Muhammad I was proclaimed

ledger.note: 1232: Muhammad I is proclaimed emir at Arjona. The inhabitants declared him emir 'after Friday prayers on 16 July 1232'; infobox 'Established: 1232'. The pages name no overlord (the Almohad Caliphate is Cliopatria's). The month is on identity.start; the event carries none so the 1232 gain below keeps the ledger in order.

region.text: Jaén, Guadix and Baeza, which 'accepted his authority quickly in 1232'

ledger.note: 1232: Jaén, Guadix and Baeza accept Muhammad I. The Emirate page also has Córdoba accept him for a few months in 1232 and Seville for one month in 1234; both 'returned to Ibn Hud's rule' (Muhammad I page), so neither is drawn.

region.text: Almería, which accepted him in 1238

ledger.note: 1238: Almería accepts Muhammad I. The Muhammad I page: 'He also took Almería in 1238'. Cliopatria's Taifa of Almería row runs to 1249 regardless.

region.text: 'stormed the city's citadel on 17 April 1238'

ledger.note: 1238: Muhammad I takes Granada. A revolt 'successfully stormed the city's citadel on 17 April 1238', and he was then 'officially declared the new ruler'. The Muhammad I page gives May 1237 in one passage and May 1238 in another; the page names no previous holder.
1238: Muhammad I makes Granada his capital. 'by invitation of the city's notables, he took Granada, which he then made his capital'; the Alhambra's foundations follow.

region.text: 'Málaga in 1239'

ledger.note: 1239: Málaga joins. 'He also took Almería in 1238 and Málaga in 1239'; the Emirate page says 'in 1238 or 1239'. The pages name no previous holder.

region.text: 'Castile besieged and captured Muhammad's hometown of Arjona'

ledger.note: 1244: Castile captures Arjona. 'In 1244, Castile besieged and captured Muhammad's hometown of Arjona.'

region.text: 'to surrender Jaén'

ledger.note: 1246: the Treaty of Jaén. Ibn al-Ahmar agreed 'to surrender Jaén and to become Ferdinand's vassal' (March 1246), with a twenty-year truce; the Muhammad I page adds an annual tribute of 150,000 maravedíes. The vassalage is recorded in the Crown of Castile dossier.

region.text: 'occupied Algeciras and Tarifa in 1275, along with Ronda further inland'

ledger.note: 1275: the Marinids occupy Algeciras, Tarifa and Ronda. 'Abu Yusuf occupied Algeciras and Tarifa in 1275, along with Ronda further inland'; that these were Granada's is my reading (the Muhammad I page puts the emirate's western end at Tarifa in 1273).

region.text: 'Málaga was given to him in 1278'

ledger.note: 1278: Málaga is given to the Marinid sultan Abu Yusuf.

region.text: 'the Marinid governor convinced ... to surrender the city to him in 1279'

ledger.note: 1279: Muhammad II regains Málaga from the Marinid governor.

region.text: 'ceded Algeciras and Ronda to the Nasrids'

ledger.note: 1294: the Marinid sultan Abu Ya'qub cedes Algeciras and Ronda to Granada. Castile had 'captured Tarifa in October 1292 and kept it'.

region.text: 'Gibraltar's Nasrid defenders surrendered after a month'

ledger.note: 1309: Castile takes Gibraltar. 'In July 1309 the Castilians laid siege to both Algeciras and Gibraltar'; 'Gibraltar's Nasrid defenders surrendered after a month' (the Emirate page: 'summer 1309'). The Strait cells stay in Cliopatria's Granada shape; this event and 1374 override them.

region.text: Ronda, 'ceded Ronda and Algeciras again in 1327 and 1328, respectively'

ledger.note: 1327: Muhammad IV cedes Ronda to the Marinids. Emirate page: 'Muhammad IV reacted to the Castilian victories by seeking an alliance with the Marinids, to whom he ceded Ronda and Algeciras again in 1327 and 1328, respectively, to use as a base' ('again' because Abu Ya'qub had given both back to Granada in 1294). The Yusuf I page shows the Marinids at Ronda in 1340: 'joined by Marinid troops from Ronda'. Mirror for marinid-sultanate (af-02), which has no Ronda event. Added by the eu-12-l repair, 2026-10-25, after the review found the losses missing.

region.text: Marbella, ceded with Ronda

ledger.note: 1327: Marbella goes with Ronda. Muhammad IV page: 'he had to surrender Ronda and Marbella, followed by Algeciras in the next year, to the Marinids'; Yusuf I page: 'In exchange for the Marinid alliance, he had to yield Ronda, Marbella and Algeciras.' The year 1327 is the Emirate page's for Ronda; Marbella is dated by the same sentence (confidence 2). Marbella is Granadan again by 1485 (Granada War: 'a base of the Granadan fleet').

region.text: Olvera, Pruna, Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime (no gazetteer entries)

ledger.note: 1327: Castile takes Olvera and its neighbours. Muhammad IV page: 'the capture of Olvera, in June 1327'; 'Subsequently, Alfonso conquered Pruna, followed by the nearby Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime' (no year of their own: read from the sequence). Mirror of crown-of-castile's gain; these are the Olvera end of the five cells Cliopatria takes from Granada only in 1333 (keyframe 1333). Replaces the missing mirror noted by the review of 2026-10-25.

region.text: Algeciras, 'ceded Ronda and Algeciras again in 1327 and 1328, respectively'

ledger.note: 1328: Muhammad IV cedes Algeciras to the Marinids (Emirate page, same sentence as Ronda; Muhammad IV page: 'followed by Algeciras in the next year'). Siege of Algeciras page: 'In 1329 the city was taken over by the King of Morocco, who made it the capital of his European domains', and 'The city was the capital and the main port of the European territory of the Marinid Empire' in 1342-1344, so Algeciras was Marinid, not Granadan, when Castile took it on 26 March 1344 (crown-of-castile /ledger/22, marinid-sultanate /ledger/17). marinid-sultanate /ledger/13 dates its gain 1329 with Castile as the counterpart; the pages opened give Granada, in 1328.

region.text: Teba (no gazetteer entry)

ledger.note: 1330: Castile takes Teba. Muhammad IV page: the siege ran July to August 1330 and 'the fortress surrendered on 30 August'; the Emirate page: 'culminating in the successful siege of Teba in 1330'. Mirror of crown-of-castile's gain; Teba is the eastern cell of the five that Cliopatria takes from Granada in 1333 (my reading of the shape).

region.text: Priego and Alcalá la Real, captured by Castile in 1342

ledger.note: 1342: Castile captures Priego and Alcalá la Real, the strip of five cells Cliopatria removes in 1344.

region.text: 'took the opportunity to recapture Al-Jazeera Al-Khadra'

ledger.note: 1369: Muhammad V recaptures Algeciras; the Moors destroyed the city in 1379.

region.text: 'In 1374 the latter handed the peninsula to the former'

ledger.note: 1374: the Marinids hand Gibraltar to Granada, 'apparently in payment for Granadan military support in suppressing rebellions in Morocco'.

region.text: Ronda and Marbella back from the Marinids (no page dates it)

ledger.note: 1374 is a bridging judgment: no page opened dates the return of Ronda and Marbella to Granada (Emirate, Ronda, Muhammad IV, Muhammad V, Yusuf I, Nasrid dynasty and Marinid Sultanate pages are silent; the Abu Inan and Abu al-Hasan pages too). What the pages give: Marinids at Ronda in 1340 (Yusuf I page, 'joined by Marinid troops from Ronda'); in 1349 'the Marinid Iberian territories were now controlled by' Abu Inan (Yusuf I page); the Marinids hand Gibraltar to Granada in 1374 (History of Gibraltar, ledger above); Ronda is Nasrid again at its fall in 1485 ('Hitherto part of the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada, Ronda was seized by the Crown of Castile in 1485', Ronda page). The year is that of the one dated Marinid hand-over, not of Ronda: a gap-filler should replace it.

region.text: Zahara de la Sierra

ledger.note: 1407: Zahara passes to Castile. Zahara de la Sierra page: 'It was ruled by Arabs until 1407.' The page does not name the conqueror or say the ruler was Granada (my reading). Mirror of crown-of-castile's gain of 1407; Cliopatria's 1402 shape swaps two cells on this edge. Setenil, also said to fall in 1407, is on no page opened.

region.text: 'he conquered the town of Antequera (1410)'

ledger.note: 1410: Ferdinand, regent of Castile, conquers Antequera. The Emirate page dates a 'War with Castile ... between 1405 and 1410'.

region.text: 'Moorish rule over Gibraltar came to an end in August 1462'

ledger.note: 1462: Castile takes Gibraltar. 'a small Castilian force' led by Alonso de Arcos, governor of Tarifa, the garrison surrendering to Juan Alonso, 'now the first Duke of Medina Sidonia'.

region.text: 'Granada launched a surprise attack against Zahara on 26 December 1481'

ledger.note: 1481: Granada seizes Zahara. 'Granada launched a surprise attack against Zahara on 26 December 1481'; the Emirate page calls it the last Granadan gain against Castile.

region.text: Alhama and the western emirate

ledger.note: 1482: the Granada War begins at Alhama. 'The seizure of Alhama and its subsequent royal endorsement is usually said to be the formal beginning of the Granada War' (infobox: February 1482 to 2 January 1492).

region.text: Alhama de Granada

ledger.note: 1482: Castilian forces take Alhama de Granada; reinforcements on 28 April averted its retaking and Ferdinand took command there on 14 May 1482.

region.text: Zahara de la Sierra

ledger.note: 1483: Castile retakes Zahara, which Granada had seized in December 1481 (the ledger above). Zahara de la Sierra page: 'It was finally captured by Castilian troops under command of Rodrigo Ponce de León, Duke of Cádiz in 1483.' Mirror of crown-of-castile's gain of 1483.

region.text: 'Ronda fell to him after fifteen days'; Marbella, 'a base of the Granadan fleet'

ledger.note: 1485: Ronda and Marbella fall. 'Ronda's fall allowed Marbella, a base of the Granadan fleet, to come into Christian hands next' (1485 for Marbella; the Ronda year is my reading from the sequence, the page gives no month).

region.text: the 'second Loja siege' of 1486

ledger.note: 1486: Loja falls after a second siege. The page names the 1486 siege; the surrender is my reading.

region.text: 'Vélez-Málaga, capitulated on 27 April 1487'

ledger.note: 1487: Vélez-Málaga capitulates on 27 April.

region.text: 'a siege that lasted from 7 May 1487 until 18 August 1487'

ledger.note: 1487: Málaga falls on 18 August after a siege that began on 7 May; al-Zagal 'lost Málaga in 1487'.

region.text: the western emirate

ledger.note: 1487: the western campaign ends with Málaga on 18 August 1487.

region.text: Baza, Guadix and Almería

ledger.note: 1489: Castile besieges Baza. The siege began in 1489 and, 'after six months, al-Zagal surrendered'.

region.text: Baza

ledger.note: 1489: Baza surrenders to Castile after the six-month siege.

region.text: 'negotiated the surrender of Almería and Guadix'

ledger.note: 1489: Almería and Guadix surrender through al-Zagal. The Emirate page says he 'negotiated the surrender of Almería and Guadix' without a year; 1489 is a bridging judgment after Baza (Cliopatria keeps them in Granada's shape to 1491). Re-checked (eu-12-l repair): the Muhammad XIII of Granada page does not mention Baza, Almería or Guadix at all ('He abdicated in 1486'); the year stays a bridge.

region.text: Baza, Guadix and Almería

ledger.note: 1489: the eastern campaign is treated as ended with the surrenders; bridging judgment, the page gives no end date for it.

region.text: the city of Granada

ledger.note: 1491: the siege of Granada begins. 'An eight-month siege of Granada began in April 1491'.

region.text: the city of Granada and its surrounding territory

ledger.note: 1492: Granada surrenders. The Treaty of Granada 'was signed on November 25, 1491' and 'the city capitulated on January 2, 1492'; Boabdil was offered 'the rulership of a small principality in the mountainous Alpujarras' and Muslims kept their religion.

region.text: the city of Granada

ledger.note: 1492: the Granada War ends with the surrender of 2 January (infobox: February 1482 - 2 January 1492).

region.text: all that remained of the emirate

ledger.note: 1492: the Emirate of Granada ends, annexed to Castile. 'On 2 January 1492, Boabdil surrendered Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella'; the last Muslim state in Iberia. Infobox 'Territorial changes: Granada annexed to Castile'; the Nasrid page: 'Deposition: 2 January 1492'.

wars.name: Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266
wars.outcome: Granada broke the peace 'in either late April or early May 1264' and supported the Muslim revolt in Castile's new lands; the Treaty of Alcalá de Benzaide (undated on the page) left Granada paying an annual tribute of 250,000 maravedíes.
wars.note: No Cliopatria shape moves; the dossier records no territorial change.

wars.name: Marinid occupation of the Strait and Málaga
wars.outcome: The Marinids occupied Algeciras, Tarifa and Ronda (1275) and Málaga (1278-1279); Castile captured Tarifa in October 1292; Abu Ya'qub ceded Algeciras and Ronda to Granada in 1294.

wars.name: Siege of Algeciras (1342-1344)
wars.outcome: Algeciras surrendered to Alfonso XI on 26 March 1344 and was incorporated into the Crown of Castile; ten-year truce with an annual tribute of twelve thousand doubloons from Granada.
wars.note: Castile also took Priego and Alcalá la Real in 1342 (Emirate page); the Battle of Río Salado (30 October 1340) preceded it.

wars.name: Castilian-Granadan war of 1405-1410
wars.outcome: Ferdinand of Antequera conquered Antequera in 1410.
wars.note: The span 1405-1410 is the Emirate page's ('War with Castile ... between 1405 and 1410'); the Ferdinand page dates only the conquest.

wars.name: Castilian capture of Gibraltar (1462)
wars.outcome: A small Castilian force took Gibraltar in August 1462, ending Moorish rule there.

wars.name: Granada War

zones.text: the western half of the emirate (Alhama, Ronda, Marbella, Loja, Vélez-Málaga, Málaga) that Cliopatria removes between its 1463 and 1487 shapes
the eastern emirate around Baza, Guadix and Almería
the city of Granada and its Vega

wars.outcome: Castilian-Aragonese victory: Alhama (1482), Ronda and Marbella (1485), Loja (1486), Vélez-Málaga and Málaga (1487), Baza and the east (1489), the Treaty of Granada (25 November 1491) and the surrender on 2 January 1492.
wars.note: A civil war between Abu'l-Hasan Ali, Boabdil and al-Zagal ran through it; al-Zagal held Málaga, Baza, Guadix and Almería at different points.

certainty.note: The Castilian frontier is approximate: no page opened gives a boundary line; the Treaty of Jaén (1246) and the Strait cells (Gibraltar, Algeciras, Tarifa) changed hands repeatedly. The coast is sharp by nature.
The front moves by siege; each conquest is a city and its district, not a line. The 1491 Treaty of Granada fixed no map.

sources.title: Emirate of Granada
sources.note: Identity, 1232 and 1492, capital, the Marinid occupations, the Algeciras, Gibraltar and Priego-Alcalá la Real dates and the Granada War outline.

sources.title: Granada War
sources.note: The 1481-1492 sequence: Zahara, Alhama, Ronda, Marbella, Loja, Vélez-Málaga, Málaga, Baza, the siege and surrender of Granada, the 25 November 1491 treaty.

sources.title: Muhammad I of Granada
sources.note: 1232 proclamation, Granada 1237/1238, Almería 1238, Málaga 1239, Arjona 1244, Treaty of Jaén 1246 and its tribute, the 1264 break, the extent at his death.

sources.title: Nasrid dynasty
sources.note: The table of emirs with reign dates; vassalage 'from 1243'; 2 January 1492.

sources.title: Siege of Algeciras (1342-1344)
sources.note: Algeciras 1344, the tribute of twelve thousand doubloons, the 1369 recapture and 1379 destruction.

sources.title: Ferdinand I of Aragon
sources.note: Antequera 1410; the page is thin on the war (1407-1410).

sources.title: Alfonso XI of Castile
sources.note: Opened for the 1333 northern-frontier cells and Priego/Alcalá la Real; silent on both (it gives only Río Salado 1340, Algeciras 1344 and the siege of Gibraltar of 1349-1350).

sources.title: Muhammad IV of Granada
sources.note: Repair pass: Ronda and Marbella surrendered to the Marinids, Algeciras the next year; Olvera June 1327, Pruna, Ayamonte, Torre Alháquime, Teba 30 August 1330.

sources.title: Yusuf I of Granada
sources.note: Repair pass: 'he had to yield Ronda, Marbella and Algeciras'; Marinid troops at Ronda in 1340; Marinid Iberian territories in 1349. Silent on Ronda's return.

sources.title: Ronda
sources.note: Repair pass: seized by the Crown of Castile in 1485, 'Hitherto part of the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada'; silent on the Marinid period and on the return.

sources.title: Zahara de la Sierra
sources.note: Repair pass: Arab rule to 1407, Granada 1481, Castile 1483.

sources.title: Muhammad XIII of Granada
sources.note: Repair pass: silent on Baza, Almería and Guadix.

sources.title: Marinid Sultanate
sources.note: Repair pass: Algeciras ceded by the Nasrids (undated), held until 1344; silent on Ronda.

sources.title: Muhammad V of Granada
sources.note: Repair pass: Algeciras recaptured 1369; no Ronda, no 1374; exile in Fez.

sources.title: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Othman
sources.note: Repair pass: Gibraltar surrendered to the Marinids on 17 June 1333; silent on Ronda.

notes:
Eight pages (budget up to 9). Cliopatria's 13 shapes (1241-1491, 31.5 k km2 falling to 13.0 k) are the Granada-Almería-Málaga core; the dossier adds Muhammad I's earlier realm (1232-1240, Jaén-Guadix-Baeza then Granada, Almería, Málaga), Jaén and Arjona (1241-1245), the Algeciras recovery of 1369-1378 and the Granada War keyframes 1482-1486 and 1490. No area figure is on any page opened; the Muhammad I page gives a 390 km east-west span (Tarifa to beyond Almería).

Places and rows to settle: (1) The Strait cells (Gibraltar, Algeciras, Tarifa) are in Cliopatria's Granada shape from 1241 to 1462, though the pages put Gibraltar with Castile 1309-1333, the Marinids 1333-1374 and Algeciras with Castile 1344-1369; the ledger overrides but the shapes were not split. (2) Cliopatria's 1363 and 1375 shapes return and then remove eight cells, including the Priego-Alcalá la Real line that the pages never return to Granada. (3) Cliopatria's Castile row holds the Jaén district and Arjona from 1236 and a ring of Seville cells from 1241, ahead of the pages (Arjona 1244, Jaén March 1246, Seville 22 December 1248): the Castile dossier adjusts. (4) The vassalage to Castile (Treaty of Jaén, 1246, 150,000 maravedíes; 250,000 after Alcalá de Benzaide; twelve thousand doubloons in 1344; 'tribute-paying vassals from 1243' on the Nasrid page; Ferdinand III page 'a tributary arrangement from Granada in 1238') is recorded as vassal_start/vassal_end in the Crown of Castile dossier; the Muhammad I page, Emirate page and Nasrid page do not agree on its start (1238, 1243, 1246). (5) Ceuta (Muhammad III captured Ceuta in 1306 or 1307 (Emirate page)) lies outside any shape and is not drawn. (6) Cliopatria's Taifa of Almería (to 1249), Taifa of Murcia and Almohad rows overlap this emirate in 1238-1249. (7) Muhammad I took Córdoba (1232) and Seville (1234) for months only. (8) Almería and Guadix: the Emirate page gives no year for their surrender; 1489 is a bridging judgment. (9) After the 1492 surrender the page does not describe the Alpujarras principality offered to Boabdil as a state.

Gazetteer names needed (coordinates used instead): places Alcalá la Real, Priego de Córdoba, Antequera, Ronda, Guadix, Baza, Baeza, Tarifa, Vélez-Málaga, Alhama de Granada, Zahara de la Sierra; region Alpujarras.

Repair pass, 2026-10-25 (eu-12-l, after the adversarial review). (1) Blocking finding fixed: Ronda and Marbella (1327) and Algeciras (1328) go to the Marinids (Emirate page: 'ceded Ronda and Algeciras again in 1327 and 1328, respectively'; Muhammad IV page: 'Ronda and Marbella, followed by Algeciras in the next year'); keyframes 1294 and 1333 are now adjust and new keyframes 1327, 1328-1329 and 1330-1332 carry the change. (2) The loss of Algeciras to Castile in 1344 is deleted: the city was Marinid ('In 1329 the city was taken over by the King of Morocco', Siege of Algeciras page); the siege stays in wars[] and the 1344, 1352, 1363 and 1369 keyframes keep Ronda and Marbella out. (3) Ronda's return is NOT on any page opened (Emirate, Ronda, Marinid Sultanate, Muhammad IV, Muhammad V, Yusuf I, Nasrid dynasty, Abu al-Hasan, Abu Inan Faris; the Spanish Ronda pages do not load): it is bridged at 1374 with confidence 1, the year of the one dated Marinid hand-over (Gibraltar), and a gap-filler should replace it; the 1374 keyframe follows. (4) The Olvera line (June 1327) and Teba (30 August 1330) now have mirror losses to Castile (Muhammad IV page), replacing the confidence-1 mirror gap. (5) Zahara: lost 1407 (Zahara de la Sierra page: 'ruled by Arabs until 1407'), seized by Granada in December 1481, lost again 1483; Setenil is on no page opened. (6) Almería and Guadix (1489): the Muhammad XIII page does not mention them; still a confidence-1 bridge. (7) Gibraltar is still not cut out of the keyframes for 1309-1373 and 1462: the ledger carries it, as before. (8) Mirror events for marinid-sultanate (af-02): gains of Ronda and Marbella 1327 and Algeciras 1328 from Granada (its /ledger/13 has Algeciras in 1329 from crown-of-castile) and the loss of Ronda and Marbella to Granada (bridged 1374).
